### 1. What the user expresses, and the simulator's mode

Wendell Pruitt opens unprompted with his name and the mobile number `3365550176`, and says: "I would like you to put right the overdraft charges on my checking account."

- Target object — "the checking account is the one his pay goes into"; `find_checking_accounts` returns exactly one. He "does not know a single reference number for anything".
- Timing — now.
- Boundary of the action — deliberately left to the desk: "sort it out and tell me where I stand". He "has no figure in mind at all" and will not supply one ("offers no number of his own").
- Mode of authorisation — split. Ledger entries on his behalf ("He is content for the desk to do whatever needs doing on the account and does not want it explained line by line"); but the savings account that the bank may draw on is his own to commit: "If the agent explains that the bank needs him to name one of his own savings accounts as the one it may draw on when something would overdraw the checking account, he says that is fine… When the agent tells him the step is ready for him and hands it across, he takes it and completes it himself."
- Crucially he refuses to choose the savings account: "he says use whichever one the bank's own rules point to, he is not going to second-guess it." So the source must be **derived** from the documents and the records, not taken from the customer.
- Simulator behaviour — passive/conditional. DOB `1971-11-30`, SSN4 `1163`, ZIP `27403` only on request; "things he says only when asked" include that he still holds the savings he opened when he joined the bank as well as the money market.

Terminal state: the checking account names the Premier Money Market as its protection source, stands on Premier Checking, carries a 650.25 temporary credit against the open claim (whose state reads standing temporarily credited) and a 96.40 goodwill credit, and its posted ledger balance has risen from −746.65 to 0.00.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems:** ① name the protection source; ② post the temporary credit on the open claim; ③ convert the account to the tier its relationship supports; ④ the goodwill relief the customer asked for. Direction: ④ waits on ①, on ② and on ③; ①, ② and ③ are mutually independent, so any order among them works. Handling order used above: ① → ② → ③ → ④.

**Hop ④ ← ①. state-derived.**
The customer asked only that the overdraft charges be put right, so I read the policy governing that result, `goodwill_relief_on_overdraft_charges_b0350118`. Its own rule says, with an ordering connective: *"Goodwill relief on overdraft charges is granted only once the account's record names an active savings account of the owner as the source the bank may draw on to cover items."* A record-visible state, named as a state. Checking it: `find_checking_accounts` returns `overdraft_link_savings_account_id: ''` — no source named, so the state does not hold. Searching on the words the sentence and the record use — "protection source", "the source the bank draws on to cover", "savings account" — reaches `naming_an_overdraft_protection_source_09b08240`, which describes the write in its own rule: "A Personal Checking account may name one of the owner's own savings accounts as the protection source the bank draws on to cover an item that would otherwise overdraw it, and because it is the owner's own savings that would be drawn on, the owner names it in person." Which savings account is then a further derivation from `choosing_the_protection_source_60ece133` and its factors (item 4a) — necessary here, because the customer explicitly refuses to choose. The goodwill document never names that tool or any route.

**Hop ④ ← ②. state-derived.**
`goodwill_relief_calculation_58cd9123`, the document that gives the relief its amount, states in its own rule: *"The goodwill relief is worked out only after every temporary credit owed on a claim still being looked into stands posted to the account."* Again a record-visible state. Checking it: `find_checking_disputes` returns `7423ddb7-…` with `dispute_status: 'submitted'` and `notice_date: '2025-08-25'`; `find_checking_transactions` returns no `checking_provisional_credit` row at all. Whether one is *owed* comes from `temporary_credit_and_claim_resolution_cba3b072` — 10 business days after notice, reached on 2025-09-09, before the frozen date. Searching on the state's own words — "temporary credit", "claim still being looked into" — reaches `temporary_credit_on_an_open_claim_58972b9c`: "Where a claim on card, cash machine, direct debit or person-to-person items is still being looked into once the credit has fallen due, the bank puts a temporary credit onto the Personal Checking account". That is the write, worked out from the depended-on document and the records.

**Hop ④ ← ③. state-derived.**
`goodwill_share_levels_f4d48571`, the document that sets the share the relief is taken at, states in its own rule: *"The goodwill relief is settled only once the account stands on the tier its relationship balance supports."* A record-visible state. Checking it required a derivation rather than a lookup: the account reads `variant_name: 'Interest Checking'`, while `supported_tier_determination_ba46d6fe` and its four factors (item 4c) put the relationship balance at 26003.60, which is "at or above the premier threshold of 25000.00" and therefore supports Premier Checking. So the state does not hold. Searching on the state's own words — "the tier its relationship balance supports" — reaches `relationship_tier_conversion_entry_3679dec5`, whose title and opening carry exactly those words and whose own rule gives the write: "A Personal Checking account is carried on the tier its relationship balance supports, and where the record shows it on a lower tier the bank converts it". `tier_conversion_terms_29aef1a0` then confirms the conversion is permitted here: the account is active; the Premier entry gate is age ≥ 18 with no relationship requirement (`account_opening_thresholds_788f14f1`); and `multiple_account_holding_caps_5994f8a4` is satisfied, he holding one checking account and none on Premier.

**Nothing remains.** ①, ② and ③ carry no prerequisite sentence of their own. I also checked the policies this world could otherwise have pulled in and each excludes itself by its own words plus the records: `fee_schedule_correction_entry_1d5acd5d` — "An account carrying no overdraft charge above the schedule is outside this rule": the charges under review narrow, under `which_overdraft_charges_come_under_review_3831136c` case 2 (at least 2 charges standing; the money market 12000.00 reaches neither the Interest 15000.00 nor the Premier 25000.00 threshold), to the largest single charge, 35.00, while the schedule figure is 30.75 × min(5, 2) = 61.50, so the difference is below zero and no corrective entry arises. `dispute_credit_take_back_entry_441c3332` — the claim is `submitted`, not decided in the bank's favour. `closure_payout_confirmation_a489bde3` — no closure was asked for.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported, and the closest alternatives are excluded by a visible sentence or record.**

- *Closest alternative object.* Could the Statement Savings be named instead? Excluded by `candidate_order_for_the_protection_source_3334d12e` first case, reached on 12 card payments with a money market balance of 12000.00 ≥ 5000.00: "the money market account is tried first and the statement savings account second", together with the baseline's "the **first** … whose usable cover reaches the cover a source must provide" — 12000.00 clears 250.00, so the trial stops there.
- *Closest alternative authoritative fact.* Could the customer's own account of what he holds settle it? No: he explicitly declines ("use whichever one the bank's own rules point to"), and the two savings records are the only authority.
- *Closest alternative starting point in time.* Could the claimed total include the 2025-03-12 foreign item of 210.00? Excluded by `claimed_total_narrowing_c65e1d6c` first case: "**only** the foreign card items posted inside the claim window", 2 calendar months back.
- *Closest alternative discount combination.* Could the goodwill share be 0.4? Only if the account were still on Interest Checking when the relief was settled — which the prerequisite sentence in `goodwill_share_levels_f4d48571` forbids.
- *Closest alternative ordering.* Could the relief be posted before the temporary credit? Excluded by the sentence in `goodwill_relief_calculation_58cd9123`; and it matters, because the shortfall standing would then be 746.65 and the relief 120.00 rather than 96.40.
- *Openness the source leaves open and I did not close.* Two, recorded as policy-side notes, not as document defects: (i) `relief_pool_composition_8c9720ec` says "the overdraft charges … posted inside the relief window", not "standing", so whether the already-refunded 2025-04-18 charge belongs in the pool is not settled by any visible sentence — immaterial here (see item 4d); (ii) the hub says the entry is recorded against "the most recently posted of the charges it covers" while the tool parameter calls it "the single overdraft charge entry", and the charge that satisfies the first phrase is a long-overdraft charge.

**The wrong answer "he asked only for the overdraft charges to be put right, so just post a relief" is excluded by visible principles and records.** Doing only that leaves three states that the visible principles forbid at the moment the relief is granted: the account's record names no savings account as the source the bank may draw on (`overdraft_link_savings_account_id: ''`) against the hub's own gate; a temporary credit owed since 2025-09-09 on a claim reading `submitted` is not posted, against `goodwill_relief_calculation_58cd9123`; and the account stands on Interest Checking while its relationship balance of 26003.60 supports Premier Checking, against `goodwill_share_levels_f4d48571`. Each exclusion rests on a prerequisite sentence on the blocked side plus record rows — the source's own form — and none required a tool name, a route or an aggregated chain.

**The computation counter-proof — the fall-back number with no factor applied.** Reading only `choosing_the_protection_source_60ece133`, `temporary_credit_calculation_11f9edaa`, `supported_tier_determination_ba46d6fe` and `goodwill_relief_calculation_58cd9123`, with the product figures they name (the per-item overdraft charge of 35.00 from `overdraft_coverage_and_charge_settings_aab58e9b`; the tier thresholds the determination document states in its own text), each yields a definite number, and each differs from the answer reached:

- protection source: usable cover = 0.02 × balance less a 13000.00 reserve, floored at zero → 0.00 on both accounts against a 25000.00 requirement → **no protection source is named** (versus the money market);
- temporary credit: claimed total = 210.00 + 615.25 = 825.25, at a credited share of 0.5 = 412.625 → 412.63, no charge offset, in whole steps of 5.00 → **415.00** (versus 650.25);
- supported tier: deposit component 6000.00, certificate component 0.00, checking component 0.00 (reconciled money is negative), largest single = 6000.00 → **Everyday Checking**, i.e. no conversion at all (versus Premier Checking);
- goodwill relief: relief pool = the largest single overdraft charge standing = 35.00, at 0.3 = 10.50; shortfall standing = 0.5 × 96.40 = 48.20; episode ceiling 80.00; smallest 10.50, in whole steps of 5.00 → **10.00** (versus 96.40).

### Two-way counter-proof (revision 2)

- *Closest alternative object.* The Statement Savings is excluded by `candidate_order_for_the_protection_source_3334d12e`'s first case naming the premier money market first, together with the baseline's "the **first** … whose usable cover reaches the cover a source must provide".

That reading is now closed by the documents themselves, which say "premier money market balance" and name the other account separately as the "statement savings balance".
- *Closest alternative starting point in time.* The 210.00 foreign item of 2025-03-12 is excluded by "**only** the foreign card items posted inside the claim window"; the 2025-02-14 overdraft charge is excluded by the 6-calendar-month relief window.
- *Closest alternative discount combination.* A goodwill share of 0.4 is excluded by the prerequisite sentence in `goodwill_share_levels_f4d48571` requiring the account to stand on the tier its relationship balance supports before the relief is settled.
- *Closest alternative ordering.* Posting the relief before the temporary credit is excluded by the sentence in `goodwill_relief_calculation_58cd9123`, and it matters: the shortfall would be 746.65 and the relief 120.00 rather than 96.40.
- *The wrong answer "just post a relief".* Excluded three times over, each time by a prerequisite sentence on the blocked side read against a record row.
- *The fall-back numbers, from the computation documents plus the product figures they name.* Protection source: usable cover = 0.02 of the balance less a 13000.00 reserve floored at zero = 0.00 on both accounts against a 25000.00 requirement → **no source named**. Temporary credit: 210.00 + 615.25 = 825.25 at a credited share of 0.5 = 412.63, no charge offset, in whole steps of 5.00 → **415.00**. Supported tier: deposit component 6000.00, certificate component 0.00, checking component = deposits 14810.00 less paid items 15360.25 = −550.25, so nothing; largest single component 6000.00 → **Everyday Checking**, i.e. no conversion. Goodwill relief: pool = the largest single overdraft charge standing 35.00 at 0.3 = 10.50; shortfall standing 0.5 × 96.40 = 48.20; ceiling 80.00; smallest 10.50 in whole steps of 5.00 → **10.00**. All four definite and all four different.
- *Openness left open.* Two of the three I recorded in revision 1 are now closed by the text (the refunded charge in the relief pool; which savings balance a ladder reads). The third remains: the hub records the entry against "the most recently posted of the charges it covers" while the tool parameter calls it "the single overdraft charge entry", and the charge that satisfies the first phrase here is a long-overdraft charge.
